newsitem.title: USA: San Jose, Calif., proposes zoning marijuana clubs.
newsitem.headline: San Jose, Calif., proposes zoning marijuana clubs.

text.p: San Jose city officials Wednesday proposed new rules that would allow pot "dispensaries" to open in commercial areas under California's medical marijuana initiative.

San Jose City Attorney Joan Gallo said her proposed zoning rules would allow people to set up pharmacy-like "medical marijuana dispensaries," where pot could be cultivated and sold in accordance with Proposition 215.
Under U.S. law, marijuana is illegal and has no approved clinical use.

But last November, voters in California approved Proposition 215 which allows sick people and their "primary caregiver" to legally possess and grow marijuana for medical use when recommended by a doctor.
Arizona voters passed a similar measure.
Gallo's proposal would allow cannabis providers in San Jose, located about 50 miles south of San Francisco, to set up shop in commercial zones, such as shopping centres, under special use permits.

"We're talking about simply having a place where medical marijuana is dispensed," Gallo said. "Proposition 215 was overwhelmingly passed and the city intends to abide by the humanitarian intent of the proposition while protecting its neighbourhoods."

Under the proposed San Jose zoning rules, the dispensaries could not be located near schools, homes, churches or day-care centres. Children would not be allowed inside and smoking pot on the premises would not be permitted.
Gallo said her zoning proposal was the first of its kind in the state.
But at least four other cities in California are crafting rules for so-called Cannabis Buyers' Clubs, which offer medical marijuana for sale, according to the group Americans for Medical Rights.
Gallo said she expected her proposal to be taken up by the San Jose city council on March 25.
